The Police Inspector of Gangammanagudi Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused No.1 and 2 for the offence punishable under Section 498(A) of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Joshna and accused No.1 was solemnized on 15-03-2021 as per Hindu tradition and customs.
At that time, the accused persons received Rs.2 lakhs, 150 grams gold ornaments and 2 KG silver articles as dowry from parents of CW1 namely CW2 Sri Manjuanth and CW3 Smt. Chandrakala.

After the marriage, CW1 was residing at house No.302, 1st Cross, Near Kusuma Stores, Abbigere Main Road within the limits of Gangammanagudi Police Station, the accused No.1 and 2 with common intention subjected the CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for fetching additional dowry amount and on 20-12-2021, the accused persons ousted her from the matrimonial house.

When she was in parental house, the accused persons went there and subjected the KABC030254032023 CC No.14096/2023 CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for fetching additional dowry amount thereby the accused persons have committed the alleged offences.

sentences.text: First Information Report:

On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1, the Sri Siddegowda, CW12/PI of Gangammanagudi Police Station registered Crime No.39/2023 against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 498(A) IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court.

4. Investigation: Thereafter, he, conducted spot mahazar on18-04-2023 as per Ex.P2, recorded the statement of requisite witnesses, collected the documents and submitted the charge sheet against accused for the alleged offences.
5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offence alleged against the accused persons.
6. The accused No.1 and 2 were enlarged on bail by the order dated 22-09-2023.
7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.
Charge:

After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused No.1 and 2, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A) of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, has been framed, read over and explained to the accused persons in the language known to them, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 12 witnesses and examined 1 witness and exhibited 2 documents.

The learned Senior APP prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused have compromised the matrimonial differences in M.C.
No.5714/2024 and hence the examination of CW2 to CW12 was dispensed with by the order dated 07-04-2025.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused persons found from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
11.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Joshna and accused No.1 was solemnized on 15-03-2021 as per Hindu tradition and customs,
at that time, the accused persons received Rs.2 lakhs, 150 grams gold ornaments and 2 KG silver articles as dowry from parents of CW1 namely CW2 Sri Manjuanth and CW3 Smt. Chandrakala as Gangammagudi Police Station vs Anil Kumar on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/77133837/
3 dowry thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.3 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
2.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage, CW1 was residing at house No.302, 1st Cross, Near Kusuma Stores, Abbigere Main Road within the limits of Gangammanagudi Police started ill-treating CW1 and KABC030254032023 CC No.14096/2023 subjected her to mental and physical cruelty thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?
3.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on the above said duration, the accused persons harassed CW1 for fetching additional dowry amount from her parental house thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act?
4. What order?
13.

The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1-3 : In the Negative Point No.4 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution KABC030254032023 CC No.14096/2023 case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution examined witness, which is as follows:
i. CW1 by name Smt. Joshna, being informant examined as PW1 and identified her signatures on Ex.P1 (Complaint) and Ex.P2 (Spot Mahazar) as Ex.P1(a) and 2(a)
deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out minor differences of opinion amongst her and the accused persons, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of Ex.P1 and Ex.P2 and further stated that she did not lodge complaint against accused persons and no mahazar was conducted in her presence.
In this regard, the learned Senior APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

On perusal of the above recital, it is appear that the disputes between the accused No.1 and CW1 (informant) have been settled.

16. This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat),
wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get KABC030254032023 CC No.14096/2023 themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused No.1 have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A) of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

17. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws (Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of KABC030254032023 CC No.14096/2023 law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws (Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offence Under Section 498(A)
of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 3 in the Negative.
